claims.source: UAP Gerb, 'Off-World Technologies Division - UAP Technology Reverse Engineering', published 17 July 2024
claims.text: A US Army Green Beret witness identified as 'RA' states that between 2013 and 2015 he was taken deep underground at a special weapons centre near Crane, Indiana to an 'Off-World Technologies Division' holding a basketball-sized sphere with an indentation and a clear tablet-like device projecting symbology, both described as weapons owing to energetic output when recovered from a craft, and both said to interact with human consciousness.
Gerb connects the division to SAIC and Sandia National Laboratories.

connections.label: 'UAP Gerb' (Sam)
connections.note: Published 17 July 2024 based on witness 'RA', a US Army Green Beret describing an underground division near Crane, Indiana holding two non-human artifacts, 2013-2015.

desc: The Off-World Technologies Division is a programme named by a first-hand witness - a US Army Green Beret identified only as 'RA' - documented in UAP Gerb's investigation of 17 July 2024. RA's account: between 2013 and 2015 he was sent to a special weapons centre near Crane, Indiana to test foreign and domestic weaponry; because he held TS/SCI clearance, a weapons instructor employed by a private contractor took him and another soldier deep underground to this division. The division is said to have held two objects not made by human hand - a sphere roughly the size of a basketball with an indentation on top, and a clear tablet-like device projecting some form of symbology. RA was told both were classified as weapons owing to energetic output when recovered from a craft, and that both interacted with human consciousness. Gerb links the division to SAIC and Sandia National Laboratories. The location matters: Crane, Indiana is the site of Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane, a real Navy facility with a genuine special-weapons and energetics mission, and the account's specificity about clearance, escort and contractor employment is the kind of detail that is checkable in principle against personnel and visitor records.
label: Off-World Technologies Division
